task: r2t4 - third-party review of t2: does the new visibility criterion actually separate hidden from visible, or did it just rename the field
headline: Overall: 成立 (sound). The fix is not a rename. I ran the runbook's own step 3.1 + 3.3 verbatim against the live landing page while the relay was connected (14:18:08.762Z) and got manual.visible=false, offsetParent=false, rect 0x0, display:none - the old ambiguous 'manual:true' is gone, replaced by an object whose visible field is false. Then I tested the other side: I captured the real landing HTML byte-for-byte from the relay (1257 bytes) and served that identical page behind a stub /health that answers edaConnected:false, matching what the real relay returns with zero windows. On that page (14:18:40.588Z) the same command returned manual.visible=true, offsetParent=true, rect 1208x21, pop 147.95x21. So the criterion discriminates in both directions and is not an 'always invisible' stub. F2 and F3 are genuinely fixed: the wait is now 4 s with the 3.994 s measured gap labelled as one observation and explicitly not an SLA, and tab selection matches URL + title, throwing when the match count is not exactly 1 instead of blind-selecting index 1. Nothing was deleted to make room for F1: the 10-row per-step timeline with edaWindowCount, the same-browser/profile requirement (5 mentions) and all three recorded failures are still present. One honest limit: the disconnected side was reproduced on the byte-identical page behind a stub health endpoint, not on the real relay in a genuine 0-window state, because the real relay held 1 window throughout my review.

criteria.claim: the new command reports invisible, and no longer emits a bare positive like manual:true
criteria.command: runbook section 3.1 verbatim (tab-list -> ConvertFrom-Json -> match url ^http://127.0.0.1:49620/landing(?:[/?#]|$) AND title -eq 'dsh-eda-bridge: register EasyEDA' -> throw if count != 1 -> dpx tab-select $landing.id), then section 3.3 verbatim (the 20-line probe here-string) via dpx eval
criteria.whyItIsNotARename: the top-level manual/pop values are now objects, so there is no boolean that can be misread as 'visible'; the decision field is manual.visible === false, and the runbook's rule says not to click on that. pop.display is 'inline-block' yet pop.visible is false, which is exactly the case a display-only check would have got wrong - the parent hides it and offsetParent/rect catch that.

criteria.claim: offsetParent !== null (plus rect/display/visibility) really distinguishes hidden from visible, and is not an always-false predicate

sideA_hidden.method: real relay, 1 window registered, real landing page

sideB_visible.method: captured the live landing HTML byte-for-byte from http://127.0.0.1:49620/landing (1257 bytes) and served that same page from a local stub on 127.0.0.1:49626 whose /health returns edaConnected:false / edaWindowCount:0 - i.e. exactly the payload the real relay produces with no window. The page logic is unmodified; only the health payload differs.
sideB_visible.result: manual.visible=true, offsetParent=true, rect 1208x21, display:block, hiddenAttr:false; pop.visible=true, offsetParent=true, rect 147.95x21
sideB_visible.consistencyWithSource: this matches the page's own code (dsh-eda-bridge.mjs: manual.hidden = !!popup && !popup.closed, only inside the not-connected branch), so the visible state is the page's real behaviour rather than something the stub invented

criteria.honestLimit: the disconnected side is a faithful reproduction (identical HTML, real page script, real not-connected branch), not the real relay observed with 0 windows - the real relay held 1 window for the whole review. I am not claiming I watched the real relay in a 0-window state.
criteria.edgeCaseNoted: offsetParent is also null for position:fixed elements, so the predicate is not universally sufficient on its own; here #manual/#pop are statically positioned, and the runbook additionally requires rect width/height > 0 and display/visibility, which covers that gap.

findings.title: running 3.3 without 3.1 probes whichever tab is bound
findings.detail: my first attempt ran the 3.3 probe while the editor tab happened to be bound (I had closed the landing tab earlier), and it returned manual.exists=false / visible=false for the editor URL. That is fail-closed and cannot produce a false 'visible', but the only signal that you are on the wrong page is the url field in the output. A one-line guard ('if result.url does not start with http://127.0.0.1:49620/landing then you are on the wrong tab - stop') would make it explicit.
findings.whyItIsMinor: section 3.1 exists precisely to bind the right tab, and section 3.3's output always prints url, so the information is present

findings.title: offsetParent is not a universal visibility predicate
findings.detail: offsetParent is null for position:fixed elements even when visible. Not an issue for #manual/#pop (static), and the probe also requires rect width/height > 0 and display/visibility, so the combined test is sound here. Worth knowing if the probe is ever copied to another page.
